title: Andoni Iraola's programme notes: 'Winning leaves you wanting more'

 9 hours ago Andoni Iraola wants more of the winning feeling as Liverpool host Chelsea in the Carabao Cup fourth round tonight.
 By Chris Shaw
 Previous Next The Reds come into the Anfield tie on the back of four consecutive victories in all competitions.
 The most recent of those was recorded last Sunday, with the in-form Brighton & Hove Albion beaten 2-0 in the Premier League.
 In his matchday programme notes for the game against Chelsea, head coach Iraola explains what pleased him most about the success over the Seagulls and how wins become addictive.
 “Straight after our game against Brighton on Sunday I was asked how happy I was that the team had made it four wins in a row and I said I was very happy,” he writes. “This is obvious of course but there is another side to winning that is also very important – it leaves you wanting more.
 “It does not matter what competition we are playing in, what team we select or what the general situation is, we always want to win and that feeling only grows when you know what it means to earn a victory.
 “It is also made bigger by the knowledge that in every game that we play our opponents will have exactly the same ambition and this will definitely be the case tonight when we play a very strong Chelsea team in the Carabao Cup.
 “This will be the second time in successive rounds that we have faced a Premier League team from London in this competition and we can expect that challenge from Chelsea to be just as aggressive as it was from Spurs. They have a squad with a lot of quality and in Xabi Alonso they have a manager whose record as a player and a coach speaks for itself.

 “Xabi is someone who I know well and someone our supporters have a lot of affection for, so I would like to offer him the warmest of welcomes in the knowledge that once the game begins no-one involved will be looking to do anyone any favours. None of us would have it any other way.
 “At the time of writing these notes it is too early to know which starting line-up we will select. First we will have to see how the players recover after the Brighton game and we will also have to consider how much freshness we can add into the team to give us the best possible chance of playing in the way we would like to.
 “During periods like this when we are playing every few days it is always a case of finding the best match-ups we can while also thinking how we are going to finish the game. This is especially true when you are playing Sunday-Wednesday-Sunday and all of the opponents are of a very high level.
 “But whatever team we pick will go out there with the same objectives that we have in every match we play. We have to show the same desire to defend our own goal, the same positive aggression in duels and the same commitment to being dangerous in transition as we did on Sunday.
 “If we do this, we will give ourselves the best possible chance of making it through to the next round.
 “The victory over Brighton showed once again the importance of doing the basics well. I love that this is something that our supporters respond to.
 “This was something I knew already from my time as an opposition manager but feeling it on this side – especially those moments when the whole crowd reacts to a tackle being won or a player showing big desire – is something that, like winning, I could never get enough of.
 “We know it will not be easy but we are looking to create more of those moments tonight. If we can do this, we will see where it takes us.”
